Add Sub-Flowline Segments to Aggregated Hydrofabric

Source: R/add_flowlines.R
add_flowlines.Rd

Takes the full-resolution reconciled flowlines (as passed to aggregate_to_distribution), splits any that exceed split_flines_meters, assigns each segment its parent aggregated flowpath_id and divide_id via the network lookup table in input_gpkg, remaps topology so the resulting segments form a valid directed graph, and attributes each segment with total and incremental contributing area derived from a flow-accumulation raster (FAC).

If events is supplied (the full event set from rf_generate_events_from_hydrolocations_fast), each event is assigned the aggregated flowpath_id and divide_id of the reconciled flowline it belongs to, and written as an events layer to input_gpkg.

Usage

add_flowlines(
  flowlines,
  input_gpkg,
  split_flines_meters = 2000,
  fac,
  fallback_fac = NULL,
  poi_events = NULL,
  junction_events = NULL
)

Arguments

flowlines

An sf object of full-resolution reconciled flowlines (the data passed to aggregate_to_distribution). Must have integer columns ID and toID, and a character column member_flowpath_id (comma-separated NHD IDs per reconciled flowline).

input_gpkg

Path to a GeoPackage produced by aggregate_to_distribution (must contain a network table). The flowlines (and optionally events) layer will be written here.

split_flines_meters

Numeric. Maximum individual segment length in metres. Default 2000.

fac

Character path to a flow-accumulation GeoTIFF, or a terra::SpatRaster already in memory.

fallback_fac

Optional character path (or NULL) to a fallback FAC raster used when fac returns NA after the standard 2-cell buffer fill. Values filled from the fallback are tagged fac_source naming that grid in the output. When fallback_fac resolves to the same file as fac (path equality, i.e. a domain configured with the fallback grid as its primary), the fallback lookup is skipped automatically. Default NULL.

poi_events

Optional sf object of snapped POI events returned by refactor_flowlines (i.e. out$events). Must contain a reconciled_id column (integer reconciled flowline ID) and poi_id. These events carry geometries repositioned onto the reconciled network.

junction_events

Optional sf object of junction events from rf_generate_events_from_hydrolocations_fast (i.e. filter(events, event_kind == "junction")). Must contain a flowpath_id column with original NHD flowline IDs.

Value

Invisibly, the sf data frame of flowline segments. The layer flowlines is written/overwritten in input_gpkg. If events is provided, an events layer is also written/overwritten.

Details

Workflow:

  1. Read the network table from input_gpkg and expand its comma-separated flowline_id column to build a per-ID lookup: reconciled flowline ID -> aggregated flowpath_id, flowpath_toid, divide_id.

  2. Split flowlines segments that exceed split_flines_meters using split_flowlines.

  3. Assign flowpath_id / divide_id to each segment via the lookup.

  4. Remap topology: segments within the same parent flowpath chain upstream-to-downstream; the terminal segment of each chain points to the first segment of the downstream chain (by flowpath_toid).

  5. Extract the FAC value at the downstream endpoint of each segment to derive tot_drainage_areasqkm (FAC * cell area in km2).

  6. Compute areasqkm (incremental) as tot_drainage_areasqkm of this segment minus the maximum tot_drainage_areasqkm of immediate upstream segments. Head segments with no upstream neighbour use their own total.

  7. If poi_events and/or junction_events are provided, each is attributed with the aggregated flowpath_id and divide_id, then the combined set is written as an events layer in input_gpkg. POI events are mapped via their reconciled_id (integer reconciled flowline ID from refactor_flowlines) directly through the network lookup. Junction events are mapped via their NHD flowpath_id column through flowlines$member_flowpath_id to the reconciled integer ID.

  8. Write flowline segments as a flowlines layer to input_gpkg and return the sf object invisibly.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
reconciled <- sf::st_read("reconciled.gpkg", "reconciled")
add_flowlines(flowlines = reconciled,
              input_gpkg = "out_vpu01.gpkg",
              split_flines_meters = 2000,
              fac = "fac.tif")
} # }
